resolved_by: Congress amended 28 U.S.C. § 46(c) in 1996 to allow senior judges to continue participating in en banc decisions, resolving the Cocke/Hudspeth split
issue: Can a federal appellate judge who takes senior status after en banc argument continue to participate in the en banc decision?

sides.position: A senior judge may continue to participate in the en banc decision even if he took senior status after oral argument
cases: United States v. Cocke, 399 F.2d 433 (5th Cir. 1968) (en banc)

sides.position: A senior judge who took senior status after en banc argument may not participate in the en banc decision, because § 46(c) limits senior-judge participation to members of the original panel
cases: United States v. Hudspeth, 42 F.3d 1013 (7th Cir. 1994) (en banc)

quote: Two years later, in 1996, Congress resolved the circuit split by amending § 46(c) to its current form.
cite: Virginia Duncan v. Rob Bonta, No. 23-55805 (9th Cir. 2025)
